overall: Tuesday, July 7 will be a stormy, cloud-dominated day in Washington, DC, with showers and thunderstorms likely throughout much of the day and into the evening. A tropical air mass in place is fueling heavy rainfall potential, active flash flood and flood watch alerts, and a persistently overcast sky that will significantly suppress daytime heating. The combination of cloud cover, wet ground, and repeated storm activity makes this a notably cooler day than the prior day's 90°F observed high.
forecast_obs_notes: Model agreement is poor with substantial spread: ECMWF is the coolest at ~77.6°F, HRRR sits at ~79.5°F, GFS at ~80.1°F, NBM at ~81.6°F, WEATHER_COM at ~81.8°F, and GEM is a warm outlier at ~84.3°F. max_temp_prediction: The active Kalshi market uses odd buckets with the top bucket at 85-86°F (10.8%), but the ensemble model's expected TMAX of 79.7°F and the notable probability mass in the low-70s buckets (74-75F: 7.8%, 72-73F: 9.5%) paint a bimodal picture — temps could land in the mid-80s if storms clear early, or stay well suppressed into the low-to-mid 70s if cloud cover and rain persist.
